input.answer: The 2016 brown-rice-based vegan diet trial enrolled participants diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and randomly assigned them to either a vegan diet excluding animal-based food including fish (n = 46) or a conventional diet recommended by the Korean Diabetes Association 2011 (n = 47) for 12 weeks; the trial measured HbA1c levels at weeks 0, 4, and 12, with the primary study endpoint being the change in HbA1c levels over 12 weeks [PMC:PMC4890770]. The 2013 aerobic versus combined exercise trial studied fourteen patients with type 2 diabetes (56±2 years) who wore a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS) during 3 days and randomly performed aerobic (AER) and combined (COMB) exercise sessions, both in the morning 24 h after CGMS placement and at least 7 days apart; the trial measured glucose variability using glucose standard deviation, glucose variance, mean amplitude of glycemic excursions (MAGE) and glucose coefficient of variation (conventional methods) as well as spectral and symbolic analysis (non-conventional methods) [PMC:PMC3594238]. In that trial, glucose levels decreased immediately after both the AER and COMB protocols by approximately 16%, a reduction sustained for approximately 3 hours, and over the 24-h period after the sessions the two exercise modalities showed similar responses for glucose levels, glucose variance and glucose coefficient of variation [PMC:PMC3594238].

sources.title: PMC:PMC3594238 · Aerobic and Combined Exercise Sessions Reduce Glucose Variability in Type 2 Diabetes: Crossover Randomized Trial
sources.text:
PMC:PMC3594238 · Aerobic and Combined Exercise Sessions Reduce Glucose Variability in Type 2 Diabetes: Crossover Randomized Trial

Baseline fasting glycemia was 139±05 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.9±0.7%. Glucose levels decreased immediately after AER and COMB protocols by ∼16%, which was sustained for approximately 3 hours. Comparing the two exercise modalities, responses over a 24-h period after the sessions were similar for glucose levels, glucose variance and glucose coefficient of variation. In the symbolic analysis, increases in 0 V pattern (COMB, 67.0±7.1 vs. 76.0±6.3, P = 0.003) and decreases in 1 V pattern (COMB, 29.1±5.3 vs. 21.5±5.1, P = 0.004) were observed only after the COMB session.

sources.text:
PMC:PMC4890770 · Effect of a Brown Rice Based Vegan Diet and Conventional Diabetic Diet on Glycemic Control of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A 12-Week Randomized Clinical Trial

Participants diagnosed with T2D were randomly assigned to follow either a vegan diet (excluding animal-based food including fish; n = 46) or a conventional diet recommended by the Korean Diabetes Association 2011 (n = 47) for 12 weeks. HbA1c levels were measured at weeks 0, 4, and 12, and the primary study endpoint was the change in HbA1c levels over 12 weeks.

sources.title: PMC:PMC3594238 · Aerobic and Combined Exercise Sessions Reduce Glucose Variability in Type 2 Diabetes: Crossover Randomized Trial
sources.text:
PMC:PMC3594238 · Aerobic and Combined Exercise Sessions Reduce Glucose Variability in Type 2 Diabetes: Crossover Randomized Trial

Both AER and COMB exercise modalities reduce glucose levels similarly for a short period of time. The use of non-conventional analysis indicates reduction of glucose variability after a single session of combined exercises.

sources.title: PMC:PMC4890770 · Effect of a Brown Rice Based Vegan Diet and Conventional Diabetic Diet on Glycemic Control of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A 12-Week Randomized Clinical Trial
sources.text:
PMC:PMC4890770 · Effect of a Brown Rice Based Vegan Diet and Conventional Diabetic Diet on Glycemic Control of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A 12-Week Randomized Clinical Trial

Both diets led to reductions in HbA1c levels; however, glycemic control was better with the vegan diet than with the conventional diet. Thus, the dietary guidelines for patients with T2D should include a vegan diet for the better management and treatment. However, further studies are needed to evaluate the long-term effects of a vegan diet, and to identify potential explanations of the underlying mechanisms.
